correctness.rationale: For a simplex with Gram matrix \(G\), nonobtuseness is equivalent to \(G^{-1}\) having nonpositive off-diagonal entries and nonnegative row sums. Cube symmetries reduce the finite check to origin-containing binary simplices. Fresh exhaustive exact-rational enumeration found local-condition counts \(17,150,1872\) in dimensions \(3,4,5\), respectively, with zero globally obtuse cases; orbit double counting gives unrestricted counts \(34,480,9984\). For the displayed dimension-six witness, every one of its \(35\) tetrahedral faces is nonobtuse, while the full inverse Gram matrix has six positive off-diagonal entries and negative row sums in rows \(2,5,6\), so the simplex is not globally nonobtuse. Thus dimension six is the first failure.
residual_risks: The theorem is a complete finite cutoff for dimensions at most six, not a classification of all dimension-six counterexamples or higher-dimensional behavior.
